answer.reason: In EIA State Electricity Profiles, Table 1 splits net generation between 'Electric Generators' (utility-owned plants) and 'IPP & CHP' (independent power producers and combined heat and power). New Jersey's generation fleet is dominated by merchant/IPP plants (e.g., PSEG Power's nuclear and gas units), while the state's regulated utilities own almost no generation, so the IPP & CHP row must be the large value. The two options are numerically consistent as the two components of the same table (they sum to a plausible total of ~60.2 million MWh), with 263,583 MWh (~0.26 TWh) matching the tiny utility-owned 'Electric Generators' share (e.g., PSE&G's small solar holdings) and 59,911,662 MWh (~59.9 TWh) matching the dominant IPP & CHP share.
